task: Enable the gomod package ecosystem in .github/dependabot.yml together with the automation its own comment names as the precondition (part of #26)

events.summary: Scoped to .github/dependabot.yml (add the gomod ecosystem, rewrite its own comment) and one new dedicated workflow, .github/workflows/dependabot-licenses.yaml. .github/workflows/ci.yaml and release.yaml are explicitly out of scope -- other lanes own them and neither needed a change: ci.yaml's License Check job already does the right thing once the inventory arrives current, it just has no way to regenerate it itself on a dependency PR.

Confirmed the defect named in dependabot.yml's own comment and in issue #26's first maintainer comment: nothing regenerates THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md on a dependency PR, so the gomod ecosystem could not be enabled. Read scripts/ci/check-third-party-licenses.sh (the 'check' mode used by ci.yaml's License Check job fails with 'THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md is stale -- run make license and commit the result' whenever go.mod/go.sum drift from the committed inventory) and the Makefile license target (bash scripts/ci/check-third-party-licenses.sh write, then go-licenses check against hack/allowed-licenses.txt). Every Dependabot Go-module PR only touches go.mod/go.sum, never THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md, so every such PR would arrive with the License Check job red on day one -- confirmed by re-running scripts/ci/check-third-party-licenses.sh check locally with the current inventory (passes, proving the file is not already stale for reasons unrelated to a dependency bump) and by inspection: no existing job or script writes that file except a human running make license by hand.

Current design (superseding the discarded single-job version this event originally described): three jobs share one pull_request trigger scoped to go.mod, go.sum, and this workflow file itself, so the read-only half runs on any same-repo PR touching those paths, not only Dependabot's. `regenerate` (contents:read, if: same-repo only) checks out the PR head, runs `make license` (the same regeneration + allowlist-check tooling CI uses, so a genuine disallowed-license finding still fails the job instead of being silently committed), and uploads THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md as a build artifact -- Harden Runner's allowlist for this job now also carries results-receiver.actions.githubusercontent.com and *.blob.core.windows.net, the endpoints upload-artifact v4 actually needs (per GitHub's own runner communication-requirements docs), on top of the go-licenses domains that are byte-identical to ci.yaml's License Check job. `verify-download` (contents:read, needs: regenerate with an explicit needs.regenerate.result == 'success' guard) downloads that artifact and prints `git --no-pager diff --stat` against the checked-out file -- observability only, never commits, and runs for the same same-repo PRs as `regenerate` so the download half of the pipeline is exercised on ordinary PRs too. `commit` (contents:write, same needs.regenerate.result guard, additionally gated to github.actor == 'dependabot[bot]') downloads the artifact again and, only if it differs from what is already committed, pushes it back onto the Dependabot branch -- preferring secrets.DEPENDABOT_LICENSE_TOKEN (a fine-grained PAT) via actions/checkout's token:, falling back to GITHUB_TOKEN with an explicit ::warning:: (never failing) when the secret is absent, and appending a '[dependabot skip]' commit-message paragraph so Dependabot keeps rebasing the branch. The write token in `commit` never coexists with a job that executes code from the PR head. Rewrote dependabot.yml's gomod comment to state the precondition inline (the comment it previously pointed at via 'noted above' was deleted by this same PR) and added the gomod ecosystem itself (weekly, commit-message prefix 'build' matching the docker entry's build-input rationale, minor/patch grouped into one PR, majors left individual for manual review since a Go major can break the API). A concurrency group serializes runs per PR with cancel-in-progress: false, so the synchronize event the commit job's own push causes cannot cancel the run that just pushed.

python3 -c yaml.safe_load on both changed YAML files parsed cleanly; actionlint on the new workflow produced no findings; bash -n and shellcheck on the embedded shell (via the workflow's own run: blocks, which is plain git plumbing, no scripts/ci/*.sh file was touched) were clean. The existing self-test suite scripts/ci/test-check-third-party-licenses.sh -- unrelated to this change but exercising the same script the new workflow's `make license` step depends on -- still passes 15/15 after this change (nothing in scripts/ci was touched). make license ran locally with network open: go-licenses needed live egress to proxy.golang.org/golang.org/etc. to resolve module license URLs (consistent with the License Check job's own allowlist, which this workflow mirrors), completed successfully, and left THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md byte-identical (git diff --stat empty) -- proving the regeneration command the new workflow calls is the one that actually works, and that the current inventory was not already stale.
events.scope: YAML validity, actionlint, the pre-existing license self-test suite, and a real local run of the exact `make license` command the new workflow invokes. Does not cover the workflow's own trigger/gating/commit-back logic running inside real GitHub Actions against an actual Dependabot PR -- that cannot be exercised locally.

events.summary: Took the precondition framing ('enable gomod only together with automation that regenerates the inventory in the same PR') and the constraint that gomod was deliberately excluded specifically because of License Check staleness from issue #26's first comment and from dependabot.yml's own pre-existing comment. Also confirmed via #26's later advisory comments that a from-scratch Renovate-based redesign (14-day cooling-off, CODEOWNERS gate, module-graph diff review) was raised only as a separate, larger, not-yet-decided proposal for a different sub-item of #26 (dependency diff review / cooling-off), not a supersede of the dependabot-based approach this task implements -- read in full before designing to avoid conflating the two.

An independent (opus) security review of the first version of this change (PR #108) found two real defects and one structural weakness the local verification in e4 could not have caught, since none of it exercises real GitHub Actions runtime semantics: (HIGH-1) a commit pushed with the default GITHUB_TOKEN does not trigger new workflow runs, so the regenerated commit would get NO CI, and main has no branch protection (confirmed: `gh api repos/dasomel/nfs-quota-agent/branches/main/protection` returns 404), so an unreviewed commit could be merged; (HIGH-2) Dependabot stops auto-rebasing a branch once it carries a foreign commit unless that commit's message contains the literal string '[dependabot skip]', which the original commit message lacked; (MEDIUM-1) the single job held contents:write while also executing `make license` against dependency-updated code from the PR head, which is the wrong order for a job holding a write token. Accepted all three plus the accompanying MEDIUM-2 (concurrency guard for grouped-update multi-push races) and LOW findings (header rationale correction, dependabot.yml comment pointing at a deleted comment, allowlist description precision); fixed in e7.
events.provenance: independent opus security review on PR #108

events.summary: Split the single job into `regenerate` (contents:read, checks out head, runs `make license`, uploads THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md as a build artifact, never touches a write token) and `commit` (needs: regenerate with an explicit `needs.regenerate.result == 'success'` guard since a custom if: replaces the implicit success() gate, contents:write, checks out head again, downloads the artifact, commits and pushes -- never runs Go tooling or any other PR-head code). The write token and PR-head code execution no longer coexist in the same job (MEDIUM-1). The commit step now prefers `secrets.DEPENDABOT_LICENSE_TOKEN` (a fine-grained PAT, contents read/write scoped to this repo, expected under Settings -> Secrets and variables -> Dependabot -- documented in the workflow header and required in the PR body) via actions/checkout's `token:`, so the resulting push triggers a normal synchronize run instead of the token-suppressed one; if the secret is absent it falls back to `github.token` and emits `::warning::` naming the manual-approval consequence rather than failing (HIGH-1). Because `secrets` is not a valid context in a step-level `if:`, the presence check is computed once in job-level `env: HAS_LICENSE_PAT` where `secrets` is allowed, then read back via `env.HAS_LICENSE_PAT` in the step if:. Verified the loop-safety claim still holds with a PAT: the pushing identity becomes the PAT's owner (never dependabot[bot]) exactly as it was github-actions[bot] under GITHUB_TOKEN, so the existing `github.actor == 'dependabot[bot]'` guard on both jobs terminates the loop either way. The commit message gained a second `-m '[dependabot skip]'` paragraph so Dependabot keeps rebasing the branch (HIGH-2); a `concurrency: {group: dependabot-licenses-<pr-number>, cancel-in-progress: true}` block was added so a grouped update's several pushes in quick succession cannot race the commit job against itself (MEDIUM-2). Corrected the header comment's self-termination rationale to name the approval-required GITHUB_TOKEN-push state and the PAT-owner actor explicitly, reworded dependabot.yml's gomod comment (it referenced 'the precondition noted above', a comment this same PR had deleted) to state the precondition inline, and corrected the allowlist comment to say it is byte-identical to ci.yaml's License Check job rather than merely 'mirrors' it.

python3 -c yaml.safe_load on both changed files (dependabot.yml, dependabot-licenses.yaml) parsed cleanly after every edit. actionlint initially caught a real defect introduced while fixing HIGH-1: `if: ${{ secrets.DEPENDABOT_LICENSE_TOKEN == '' }}` on a step is invalid -- 'context "secrets" is not allowed here' -- fixed via the job-level env indirection described in e7, then actionlint re-run clean (exit 0). A second self-inflicted defect -- a literal blank line before '[dependabot skip]' inside a `run: |` block scalar at column 0, which YAML parsed as ending the block scalar early and then failed to parse the orphaned text as a new node -- was caught by the yaml.safe_load step itself and fixed by moving to a second `-m` argument on one line. bash scripts/ci/test-check-third-party-licenses.sh still passes 15/15 (script itself untouched by any of these fixes). `make license` was not re-run since the split job's `make license` step and its egress allowlist are unchanged from the version already verified in e4 -- only job topology, token selection, and commit-message wrapping changed around it.
events.scope: YAML validity and actionlint across both changed files after the split-job/PAT-fallback/dependabot-skip/concurrency changes, plus re-confirming the pre-existing license self-test suite is unaffected. Does not re-verify `make license` execution (unchanged since e4) or, as before, the workflow's real trigger/token/commit-back behavior inside GitHub Actions against an actual Dependabot PR -- the PAT path in particular has never executed for real, since PR-time review cannot provision or exercise the DEPENDABOT_LICENSE_TOKEN secret.

events.summary: gomod is enabled in .github/dependabot.yml with the regeneration automation its own comment named as the precondition now in place. The two defects and structural weakness an independent security review found in the first version (PR #108) are fixed per e7, at the evidence level in e8; the PAT-based commit-back path and the plain-GITHUB_TOKEN fallback path have each been statically validated but neither has executed against a real Dependabot PR, named as the remaining risk in e10.

Complete at the design, static-validation, and local-tooling-run level described in e4 and e8, including the post-review fixes in e7. Unverified: the commit-back workflow -- either token path -- has not executed against a real Dependabot-opened PR in GitHub Actions (cannot be exercised outside CI, and the DEPENDABOT_LICENSE_TOKEN secret does not yet exist in the repository), so its trigger condition, permissions, PAT-vs-fallback branching, and push-back-onto-the-PR-branch behavior are unconfirmed until the first real gomod Dependabot PR arrives after a maintainer adds the secret; this is the concrete remaining risk, not a hidden gap.

A second round of independent security review on PR #108 (after the HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW fixes in e6/e7 landed) found one new HIGH: actions/upload-artifact and actions/download-artifact v4 talk to the Actions Results Service and Azure Blob Storage, and neither job's Harden Runner allowlist (byte-identical-to-ci.yaml on `regenerate`, github.com/api.github.com-only on `commit`) included those hosts -- ci.yaml has no artifact step, so there was no existing entry to copy. Under egress-policy: block both artifact steps would fail, so the commit-back would never happen and every Dependabot PR would be red again, the exact failure mode this workflow exists to prevent. The review also required making the fix observable on this PR itself rather than leaving it as 'unverified until a real Dependabot PR arrives': widen the trigger so a read-only regenerate+verify-download pair runs on any same-repo PR touching go.mod/go.sum/this workflow file, add a dedicated dry-run verify-download job, and flip concurrency.cancel-in-progress to false since the commit job's own push was cancelling the run that had just pushed.
events.provenance: independent opus security review, second pass on PR #108 at commit e9746a6

events.summary: Looked up GitHub's own self-hosted-runner communication-requirements documentation (not a third-party aggregator) for the exact hostnames actions/upload-artifact and actions/download-artifact v4 require: results-receiver.actions.githubusercontent.com and *.blob.core.windows.net, both listed under 'Artifacts, logs, and caches'. Added both to the Harden Runner allowlist on every job that uploads or downloads the artifact (`regenerate`, the new `verify-download`, and `commit`). Restructured the trigger to `pull_request` with paths [go.mod, go.sum, .github/workflows/dependabot-licenses.yaml] and dropped the dependabot[bot] actor restriction from `regenerate`'s if: (kept only the same-repo check), so the upload half runs on any same-repo PR matching the filter -- including this PR, which touches the workflow file itself. Added `verify-download` (contents:read, needs: regenerate, same same-repo guard) which downloads the artifact and runs `git --no-pager diff --stat` against the checked-out THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md, never committing -- this is what lets the download half be observed on a normal PR too. `commit` keeps its dependabot[bot] gate (it is the only job that writes) and its own needs.regenerate.result == 'success' guard, now alongside the same two artifact-service allowlist entries. Set concurrency.cancel-in-progress to false so the commit job's own PAT-triggered synchronize run cannot cancel the run that just pushed it. Rewrote e3 above and this workflow's header comment to describe the current three-job design instead of the discarded single-job one.

python3 -c yaml.safe_load parsed the restructured workflow cleanly; actionlint reported no findings (exit 0) after the job split, trigger change, and allowlist additions. bash scripts/ci/test-check-third-party-licenses.sh still passes 15/15 (script untouched). Pushed the change and observed the real dependabot-licenses.yaml run on this PR under Harden Runner's egress-policy: block: the `regenerate` job's 'Upload regenerated inventory' step and the new `verify-download` job's 'Download regenerated inventory' step both completed successfully -- the exact two network calls (upload-artifact, download-artifact) the review flagged as unreachable under the old allowlist -- with no blocked-endpoint entries in the Harden Runner insights for either job. verify-download's 'Show diff against the committed inventory' step printed an empty `git diff --stat` (0 files changed), confirming the artifact round-trip reproduced THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md byte-for-byte and that the file was not already stale for this PR. The `commit` job correctly did not run (its dependabot[bot] actor guard is false for this human-authored PR), so the push/PAT-fallback path remains unverified against a real Dependabot PR, as before.
events.scope: YAML validity, actionlint, the pre-existing license self-test suite, and -- new for this round -- an actual GitHub Actions run of this PR's own dependabot-licenses.yaml showing the upload-artifact and download-artifact steps both succeed under Harden Runner's block policy with the corrected allowlist, plus the resulting diff-stat evidence. Does not cover the commit job's push (still gated to dependabot[bot], never exercised by this PR) or the DEPENDABOT_LICENSE_TOKEN PAT path, since that secret does not exist in the repository yet.

events.summary: gomod is enabled in .github/dependabot.yml with the regeneration automation its own comment named as the precondition now in place. All defects found across two rounds of independent security review on PR #108 are fixed, and for this round the fix is directly observed: this PR's own dependabot-licenses.yaml run shows the upload-artifact and download-artifact steps succeeding under Harden Runner's block policy, per e13. The push/commit path (gated to dependabot[bot]) remains the one part of the pipeline that has never executed for real, named in e15.

Complete at the design, static-validation, and now real-CI-run level described in e4, e8, and e13. The artifact upload/download path that the second security review flagged as would-fail-under-block is now directly observed succeeding on this PR, closing that gap. Unverified: the `commit` job's push -- via either the DEPENDABOT_LICENSE_TOKEN PAT or the GITHUB_TOKEN fallback -- has still never executed against a real Dependabot-opened PR, since that job is gated to github.actor == 'dependabot[bot]' and this PR is human-authored; the PAT secret also does not exist in the repository yet. This is the concrete remaining risk, not a hidden gap, and will only be closed by the first real gomod Dependabot PR after a maintainer adds the secret.
